title: Northern Harrier — hunting in snow
subtitle: A northern harrier in low flight over snow at Barr Lake, Colorado, talons reaching forward to grasp some brush. Bright, almost featureless snow surfaces alongside finely barred wing and tail feathers give noise-reduction tools a wide tonal range to handle.
editor_note: I disagree with darwain on this one — Lightroom Denoise looks too soft to me (more like a 3 than a 5), and Topaz Photo is the strongest of the set in my view.
exif_summary: OM-1 with M.150-400mm F4.5 TC + MC-14 at 700mm, 1/2000s at f/8, ISO 500

images.title: RAW
images.caption: Original RAW image, which is quite soft.

critique.text: As the original RAW image (.ORF), this establishes the baseline for the set. The image suffers from significant visible noise throughout, most noticeably as a grainy texture across the white snow and color noise in the darker plumage of the bird. The main subject is also noticeably soft, likely due to high ISO degradation. Overview of the set: All edited versions successfully remove the distracting noise. The standard DNG edits (Images 1 & 2) offer a good balance of noise reduction and moderate sharpening. The 'Smart Photo' (Image 4) provides aggressive sharpening but looks slightly artificial, while the DxO DeepPRIME version (Image 6) yields the best overall result, extracting incredible detail while cleanly removing noise. Because the noise is so prominent and the subject is soft here, the overall quality of this specific unedited file is poor.

images.title: DxO PureRAW 6
images.caption: Dxo using DxO DeepPrime wD3 with Lens Sharpness Optimization increased to 200

critique.text: Processed with DxO DeepPRIME XD3, this image represents the best balance of noise reduction and sharpening in the entire set. The heavy noise seen in the raw file has been completely eliminated, resulting in a beautifully clean snowy background. Most impressively, it has extracted an incredible amount of sharp, natural-looking detail from the bird's feathers, face, and talons, avoiding the artificial, over-sharpened look seen in the 'Smart Photo' edit. The overall image quality is excellent, successfully rescuing the noisy, soft raw file and turning it into a crisp, highly impactful photograph.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with default noise reduction ans subject sharpening using lens blur at setting of 50

critique.text: Very similar in appearance to the first processed DNG, this image successfully eliminates the heavy luminance and color noise present in the raw file. The sharpness is good, making the bird stand out reasonably well against the snowy background. However, when compared side-by-side with the DxO processed image, the fine details in the feathers appear slightly softer and less defined. It is a vast improvement over the unedited original, serving as a cleanly standard noise-reduced file.

images.title: Topaz Photo 2x upsized
images.caption: This uses Topaz Photo with noise reduction, subject sharpening with lens blur, and 2x upsizing

critique.text: This processed DNG shows a significant reduction in noise compared to the original RAW file. The snow is completely clean, and the color noise on the bird is gone. Sharpness has been improved, pulling more detail out of the bird's wings and face, though it lacks the ultra-fine detail extraction seen in the more advanced AI edits in this set. It represents a solid, balanced edit that greatly improves overall image quality without introducing severe artifacts.

images.title: ON1 RAW
images.caption: ON1 RAW with NoNoise and TackSharp

critique.text: The 'Smart Photo' processing applied here, likely using an AI enhancement tool, has completely eradicated the background noise and heavily sharpened the subject. The bird is strikingly sharp relative to the original RAW, with individual feathers and talons highly defined. However, this aggressive sharpening comes at a cost: the image has an unnatural, 'crunchy' and almost plastic appearance, especially along the high-contrast edges of the wings. While the main subject is much sharper than the raw file, the over-processed look detracts from the overall natural feel of the image.

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom AI Denoise at default settings

critique.text: This image appears to be an identical unedited copy of the original RAW file, exhibiting the exact same baseline characteristics. It features heavy, distracting noise across the entire frame, particularly visible against the high-key snowy background. The subject remains soft, lacking the crisp definition necessary to make a wildlife shot truly stand out. With no noise reduction or sharpening improvements applied, it shares the lowest overall quality rating in this set.
